name: Vulnerability Scanning & Assessment
tagline: Automated detection of known CVEs and misconfigurations at scale, plus manual triage.

tools.name: Nuclei
tools.desc: Template-driven scanner (projectdiscovery) running thousands of YAML checks against your web, network, and infrastructure targets to confirm known CVEs and misconfigurations.
tools.when: First-pass automated sweep across a whole asset list; fast and CI-friendly enough to run on every build.

tools.name: Nessus
tools.desc: Tenable's market-standard commercial scanner with credentialed and remote checks across OSes, services, and web; the free Essentials tier covers a small lab.
tools.when: Deep credentialed findings and compliance-style reports on the servers you operate.
tools.install: sudo dpkg -i Nessus-10.x-ubuntu.deb  (free Essentials .deb from tenable.com)

tools.name: OpenVAS (GVM)
tools.desc: Greenbone's open-source stack forked from the old Nessus; schedules scans of thousands of network vulnerability tests (NVTs) with a web dashboard.
tools.when: Self-hosted, ongoing internal-network scanning without commercial licensing.
tools.install: sudo apt install gvm && sudo gvm-setup

tools.name: Vuls
tools.desc: Agentless Go scanner that runs from one control host over SSH to inventory OS packages, middleware, and containers, then maps each server to applicable CVEs.
tools.when: Fleet-level Linux vulnerability tracking when installing agents on every box is not an option.

tools.name: Nikto
tools.desc: Perl web server scanner running 7,000+ checks for known files, outdated software, and misconfigurations on your own sites.
tools.when: Fast baseline sweep of a web server's exposed surface before deeper application testing.

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.desc: Full-featured open-source web app scanner combining an intercepting proxy, spidering, and automated active and passive scanning behind a REST API.
tools.when: DAST runs against the apps you build, or as the intercepting proxy for manual test sessions.

tools.name: Arachni
tools.desc: Feature-rich Ruby web app scanner with modular platform checks, a REST API, and distributed scanning of your own applications.
tools.when: Headless or scripted scans that need to scale across many of your endpoints from one controller.
tools.install: Download and extract the arachni release archive from GitHub

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.desc: Long-standing automated SQL injection detector with database fingerprinting; validates whether a suspected injection point on your own app is genuinely exploitable.
tools.when: Confirming and triaging reported SQLi findings on applications you own and operate.

tools.name: Nettacker
tools.desc: OWASP automation framework that scans your networks in layers (ports, services, subdomains), correlates the results, then runs follow-up module checks.
tools.when: Automating broad network discovery plus vulnerability checks against your own infrastructure in one pass.

tools.name: Vulners
tools.desc: Aggregated vulnerability and exploit database offering a free API plus an Nmap script that matches your scanned services against millions of CVEs.
tools.when: Enriching plain nmap service banners of your hosts with live CVE matches at no cost.
tools.install: Copy vulners.nse into /usr/share/nmap/scripts/ (get it from vulners.com)

tools.name: OpenSCAP
tools.desc: NIST-certified scanner applying security-policy content (CIS, STIG) and OVAL CVE definitions to your Linux hosts for compliance and vulnerability posture.
tools.when: Auditing your servers against published baselines and tracking CVE coverage across them.

tools.name: WPScan
tools.desc: WordPress scanner that fingerprints core, theme, and plugin versions against the WPScan vulnerability database and does user and weak-password checks.
tools.when: Regularly auditing the WordPress sites you maintain for outdated plugins and known CVEs.

tools.name: CMSmap
tools.desc: Python tool that scans WordPress, Joomla, and Drupal sites you own for known vulnerabilities and exposed file paths.
tools.when: A single-command health check across mixed small-CMS estates without installing separate scanners.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/Dionach/CMSmap && cd CMSmap && python3 cmsmap.py

tools.name: droopescan
tools.desc: Lightweight Perl scanner focused on Drupal, with partial WordPress and Bolt coverage; strong on plugin and module fingerprinting.
tools.when: Targeted assessments of the Drupal sites in your fleet.

tools.name: Trivy
tools.desc: Aqua's scanner that fingerprints vulnerable packages and CVEs in the container images, filesystems, IaC templates, and SBOMs you run.
tools.when: Adding vuln gates to your image builds and scanning local containers for known CVEs before deployment.

tools.name: Grype
tools.desc: Anchore's fast scanner pairing with Syft to map dependency CVEs across the containers and filesystems you build and ship.
tools.when: Container and directory scans where you also want an SBOM generated in the same workflow.

tools.name: osv-scanner
tools.desc: Google's scanner that matches your project lockfiles and SBOMs against the open-source-focused OSV.dev vulnerability database.
tools.when: Quick CI check of dependency lockfiles in your own repos against a community-maintained vuln feed.

tools.name: cve-bin-tool
tools.desc: Scans binary files and their strings to identify which known-vulnerable library and product components your software bundles.
tools.when: Checking compiled products you distribute for embedded third-party components with published CVEs.

tools.name: searchsploit / Exploit-DB
tools.desc: Offline grep over the ~40,000-entry Exploit-DB archive bundled with Kali, showing exploit scripts, Metasploit modules, and build instructions for your own lab.
tools.when: Looking up local proof-of-concept code to reproduce and verify a CVE on systems you control.

tools.name: cve-search
tools.desc: Local MongoDB-backed engine that ingests NVD, CISA, and Exploit-DB feeds for fast bulk lookups across your whole inventory.
tools.when: Correlating a large asset list against CVE data offline when you cannot rely on external APIs.

tools.name: NVD (NIST)
tools.desc: Official NIST vulnerability feed and web UI; the reference source for CVE metadata, CPE mappings, and CVSS metrics.
tools.when: Confirming identifiers, severity scores, and affected product lists for a CVE under review.
